messages.subject: Question About Random Forest With Cross Validation
parts:
Hi, group,

I implement my own random Forest code based on this blog
http://blog.cloudera.com/blog/2013/02/how-to-resample-from-a-large-data-set-in-parallel-with-r-on-hadoop/

But I find it seems fail to run randomForest on entire data set that has the same key.

Here is my data format:

            PROTEIN    y    x1       x2       x3       x4       x5    x6       x7       x8
1    ADT1_YEAST    3    0.58    0.61    0.47    0.13    0.5    0.00    0.48    0.22
2    ADT2_YEAST    3    0.43    0.67    0.48    0.27    0.5    0.00    0.53    0.22
3    ADT3_YEAST    3    0.64    0.62    0.49    0.15    0.5    0.00    0.53    0.22
4    AAR2_YEAST    2    0.58    0.44    0.57    0.13    0.5    0.00    0.54    0.22
5    AATM_YEAST    3    0.42    0.44    0.48    0.54    0.5    0.00    0.48    0.22



Here is my code:

library(rmr2)

num.models = 4000
seed0 = 122

# this function is used to randomly divide data into K fold.
f.idgenerator <-function(data=yeast_df,K=10,seed0=123){
    y=data[,"y"]
    id=rep(0,length(y))
    tn=names(table(y))
    set.seed(seed0)
    for (i in 1:length(tn)) {
        nn=sum(y==tn[i])
        tt=c(rep(1:K,floor(nn/K)),sample(1:K,nn-K*floor(nn/K)))
        tt=sample(tt)
        id[y==tn[i]]<-tt
        }
    id
}

# map function -> generate num.models duplicates of data sets
my.subsample <- function(k,input) {
    generate.sample <- function(i) {
        keyval(i, input)       
    }
    c.keyval(lapply(1:num.models, generate.sample))
}

# reduce functin -> for each data set, do 10 fold cross validation with randomForest classifier
my.fit.trees<-function(k, v) {
    res=v$y
    pres0=rep(0,length(res))
    pres01=pres0
    tres01=res
    tjd=f.idgenerator(data=v,K=10,seed0=k)
    for (j in 1:10) {
        x<-as.matrix(v[tjd!=j,2:9])
        y<-factor(as.matrix(v[tjd!=j,1])) # predictor
        xtest<-as.matrix(v[tjd==j,2:9])
        ytest<-factor(as.matrix(v[tjd==j,1]))
        rf <- randomForest(x,y, ntree=1000,mtry=5,keep.forest=TRUE,type="class")
        tres01[tjd == j] <- predfn(rf, newdata=xtest,type="class")     
        pres01[tjd == j] <- apply(predfn(rf, newdata=xtest,type="prob"),1,max)
    }
    XV0<-data.frame(true=res,rf.c=tres01,rf.p=pres01)
    keyval(k,XV0)
}

#mapreduce function
mapreduce(input=to.dfs(yeast_df),
          map=my.subsample,
          reduce=my.fit.trees)

What I'm expecting is to generate 4000 copy of original data, then for each copy, do a random 10-fold cross validation, which means I'm expecting 4000 reduce calls.
But my Hadoop cluster reports 5,342,280 reduce calls, which is the total number of observations in 4000 data set. So my reducer only takes a row of observation, not a data set with the same key. Why it is so and how can I implement a 10-fold partition here?

rmr     map calls          1         
0 1
    reduce calls          0 5,342,280        
5,342,280
